- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in such contexts.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model overreacts; adjust downward by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; anticipate reversal 1–2 days ahead and slightly lower forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If true outcome is below model by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.
